SELECTED_INDEX: 1
CONFIDENCE: 0.45
EXPLANATION: Narrow band at 3301 cm⁻¹ is consistent with an N–H stretch of a primary amine rather than the broad O–H of an alcohol; strong twin C–H stretches at 2874/2907 cm⁻¹, methyl bending at 1474 and 1441 cm⁻¹, C-N stretch near 1070 cm⁻¹, and CH₃ rocking/twisting modes in the 830–920 cm⁻¹ region all match the simple spectrum expected for CH₃NH₂ (methylamine, SMILES = “CN”). Other candidates contain O–H, Si–H, B-X or longer carbon chains that should introduce additional or shifted bands (e.g., carbonyl ~1700 cm⁻¹, Si–H ~2100 cm⁻¹, etc.) not observed here. Thus candidate 1 best fits the observed Raman peaks.
